transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door hinge / balance / springs (drops open). Next: On an integrated machine check the furniture-door alignment/balance. Let me know what you find.

Not sure what you mean by alignment, but the door closes and latches fine and sits square. When I open it, the left side has a bit of tension but the right side has none at all. I also heard a twang last week when it went.

By alignment I mean whether the door sits straight and square in the opening when closed, with even gaps on both sides and the latch meeting the catch cleanly. From what you've said, it closes, latches and sits square, so the alignment sounds fine. Next: Note whether moving or pressing the door changes anything. Let me know what you find.
Pressing the door doesn't change much, it just drops open on the right side with no resistance. I had a look under the plinth with a torch and can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
The checks point to the door hinge. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on the side edge of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The sticker on the door edge is partly peeled, but I can see it starts with LTF. I can't make out the rest of it, sorry.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
The checks point to the door hinge. If the model number can't be read, it is often also on the guarantee card, the receipt or the manual; with it, the right part can be matched. Without it, an appliance engineer can identify and fit the right door hinge from the machine itself.
